game.name: Slime 3K: Rise Against Despot
game.short_description: Welcome to Slime 3K, an unhinged roguelite bullet-heaven set in the Despot’s Game universe! Build a deck of crazy weapons, grow stronger and devour hordes of pink puny humans as a murderous jelly blob on a warpath of death, violence and pretzels.

placements.verbal_evidence: I'm going to put this as a like a high seat tier

commentary.label: Tier list Part 2 (2024)
commentary.summary: Slime 3K is a horde-survival, single-level-layout roguelike that closely mirrors another game he already covered, reusing characters, enemies, animation and art. You play a very slow slime and buy weapons that just stack into an inventory, with little depth beyond that. He finds it fun at first but repetitive and shallow, since builds barely change how you play. The cute, funny art style rescues it, and he feels it needed more development time. He places it in a high tier, which the ASR renders as 'high seat tier' and most likely means high C or B.
praise: Charming, cute and funny art style that he says saves the game
Enjoyable and fun in the first runs
Satisfying to find different weapons that kill things
A few build directions exist, such as shotgun-style versus other weapon effects
criticism: Shallow inventory system: you just buy weapons and stack duplicates to level them
Very repetitive, and different builds do not change moment-to-moment play
Extremely slow slime with no mobility, unlike the genre norm where movement is key
Found an infinite-money exploit that he could repeat consistently from the fifth run
Camera sits awkwardly low, leaving the character close to the screen edge
Feels like it needed more time in development
unique_points: Being slow and tanky with no mobility is an unusual twist for the horde genre, making it all about whether weapons out-damage incoming hits
Mechanically it does little that is new, relying on its sibling game's formula
commentary.quote: the art style does save this game quite a bit
comparisons: The earlier auto-battler-style horde game from the same art lineage (name forgotten, likely Brotato-adjacent)
design_criteria: Mechanical uniqueness: little that differs from its sibling game
Build diversity: builds exist but do not change gameplay
Inventory/equipment depth: only buy and stack weapons
Art style/charm: cute and funny, the main strength
Economy balance: exploitable for infinite money

community.one_liner: A pixel-art roguelite bullet-heaven from Konfa Games and tinyBuild, set in the Despot's Game universe, where you play a murderous slime and build a deck of weapons and passive-tag synergies to survive escalating hordes across about 20 levels.
community.consensus_summary: Steam players rate it Mostly Positive (about 80% of roughly 1,700 reviews) and it is a modest, cheap ($4.99) indie hit that has not broken out; third-party estimates put it at 50-100k owners and roughly $120k gross. Fans love the art, animation, weapon variety and the deckbuilding and tag-synergy layer, which they say makes it more strategic than a typical Vampire Survivors clone. Detractors say the meta-progression is slow and grindy, builds get narrow, and later levels feel like stat checks or difficulty spikes, so the game runs out of surprises around the mid-game. It left Early Access (launched Nov 2023) with a 1.0 release on Oct 31, 2024, and recent reviews are slightly better than the all-time average (86% positive on a small sample). I found no professional critic coverage: Metacritic lists the game but has no Metascore and only a couple of user ratings. Note: the task brief says 2023, which is the Early Access date; the full release is 2024.
best_things: Pixel art, character design and animation are widely called masterful and are the most consistent praise, including from players who otherwise bounce off the game
The deckbuilding layer (choosing which weapons can appear in a run) plus a tag-synergy system gives builds real strategic weight, unlike idle-feeling survivor-likes
Weapons are varied, funny and have satisfying sound design (one reviewer singles out the shotgun audio)
Upgrades, both in-run and meta, are described as large and intuitive rather than many tiny percentage bonuses, so there is little 'number soup'
Enemy hordes flowing around obstacles and the general action/effects feel polished and fast
Every level differs and pushes you to adapt your deck, which keeps the campaign feeling fresh and gives achievement and challenge hunting to do
A soundtrack that some reviewers call top-tier, and a low price that many consider good value, especially on sale
Decent playtime for the price: a top-voted review reports nearly 30 hours and full completion
worst_things: Grindy meta-progression: upgrades and new cards are expensive and gated behind very specific unlock conditions (e.g. finish a level with several level-3 weapons of one type)
Difficulty spikes and stat-check levels, with level 10 and the later levels called out repeatedly for chaos, tanky mini-bosses and slowdown
Performance: frame drops and lag in late levels, particularly when many enemies and projectiles are on screen; a Steam discussion complains of freezes at the end of level 10
Builds feel limited: players report being pushed to a single exact deck per level, and many unlockable cards or tags feel cosmetic or weak
Weak-feeling weapons early and long stretches of repeating the same loop; one reviewer says hour 20 has little more than hour 2
Bugs and platform issues: a level-10 crash report, a macOS launch failure thread, mouse/controller input conflicts, and poor Steam Deck input handling
Boss-kill loot spawns on top of the player, which can break the 'No Hands' achievement, and boss rewards are seen as near worthless because the run ends right after
Some find the loop repetitive and unfun compared with Vampire Survivors, calling it 'mid' or boring after a few hours
improvements: Raise the five-deck save limit; players say it forces constant rebuilding and discourages experimentation
Better in-game explanation of mechanics (tags, synergies, why you are dying), since many negative reviews come from players who never discovered these systems
Rebalance difficulty spikes and the tankiness of late-level enemies and mini-bosses so not every hard level requires one specific build
Speed up or flatten the meta-progression and relax narrow unlock conditions so diverse weapons arrive before the campaign ends
Fix late-game performance, boss-loot placement, and controller/mouse/Steam Deck input options (including a setting to replace the hold-to-exit-shop button)
More powerups, loot and variety in level content (some levels feel like empty arenas with nothing to do)
unique_things: Deckbuilding bolted onto a bullet-heaven: you build a deck of weapons pre-run and levelling up opens a shop instead of offering random picks
Tag-synergy passives that reward stacking weapons of the same tag, tied to meta-upgrades that change mechanics (such as contact damage)
Weapons merge in tiers (two tier-1 weapons give a tier-2 weapon, up to A-tier), per a Metacritic user review
Roughly 20 hand-designed levels with distinct enemy waves and bosses instead of one repeating arena, and predetermined waves so skill rather than RNG decides outcomes
Twin-stick aiming with manual shooting, rather than fully auto-attack, plus optional map activities that make you roam
Dark, edgy humour in the Despot's Game universe with a murderous jelly protagonist
tedious_or_disliked: Grinding DNA/XP and resources to unlock upgrades and cards, with players repeating a farm level such as level 10
Hold-button prompts (especially to leave the shop on a gamepad) that are used very often with no option to change
Screens crowded with projectiles and enemies, making evasion hard and triggering lag
Replaying short runs against special levels (e.g. slowing-bullet level) that can instakill you
Rebuilding decks repeatedly due to the limited number of save slots
Shop-centric economy: money comes mainly from shops and drops, so weapons feel weak until you build up
divisive_points: Difficulty: fans call the bottleneck levels good forced experimentation; critics call them unfair stat checks
Deckbuilding: some see it as the game's best feature and the source of strategic depth; others find it constricts variety or simply dislike it, and one left after seeing the deckbuilder tag
Depth vs. repetition: some say every system has a purpose and rewards learning; others see the same loop executed repeatedly with shallow meta-progression
Comparison with Vampire Survivors: some call it their favourite survivor-like, others say the older game does everything better apart from the visuals
community.reception_notes: Launched in Steam Early Access in November 2023 and reached 1.0 on Oct 31, 2024, when it also appeared on consoles (Metacritic lists PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X, Xbox One, Switch and PC, published by tinyBuild). Metacritic currently shows no critic reviews and no user score (2 ratings). No OpenCritic page was found in my checks. Steam reception has stayed Mostly Positive, and recent reviews trend somewhat higher. Community discussion on Steam centres on crashes or freezes on level 10, macOS launch trouble, controller/mouse input conflicts and grinding strategies. No notable controversy found. Limitation: my web-search quota was exhausted, so I could not reach Reddit or press reviews (Reddit fetch was blocked); community findings rely on the Steam review sample and Steam community thread titles.
